subject: Post-signature onramp: deployment commitment, canary gating, and training cadence
messages:

To: Eleanor Briggs <eleanor.briggs@labsuite.ai>, Marco Silva <marco.silva@labsuite.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-signature onramp: deployment commitment, canary gating, and training cadence

Hi Eleanor / Marco —

Thanks again for signing. Attached is the initial MAP and a focused canary checklist so we can align on the first 8 weeks post-close. High-level asks for this note:

- Confirm the target canary cohort (we recommended 5% of production traffic from a single region).
- Confirm blackout windows for migration (any dates we should avoid in Aug–Sep).
- Confirm training audience and preferred cadence (train-the-trainer vs. full-seat).

What I’ve attached: MAP_Labsuite_v1.xlsx (mutual action plan with milestones), canary-checklist.pdf (technical gating & rollback), and a placeholder training-calendar.ics to propose cohort sessions.

Proposed kickoff: Thu 8/3 10:00 PT — 45 min (kickoff + outline of who does what). If that doesn’t work, suggest 8/4 same window.

Next steps from us after your confirmation: we’ll lock the canary gating thresholds, create the rollback runbook, and provision a dedicated canary pool for Labsuite on Redwood Dedicated.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Monica Patel
Head of Customer Onboarding
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Date: Wed, 01 Aug 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-signature onramp: deployment commitment, canary gating, and training cadence

Thanks Monica — really clear. A few clarifying items before we lock dates: 

1) Can you confirm the expected sequence-length and average request size you used to estimate the canary pool capacity? Our production sequences average ~900 tokens for inference requests (multi-turn support included).

2) For blackout windows: we have a vendor maintenance freeze on 8/15–8/18 and a company-wide all-hands on 9/7 (please avoid those).

3) Data residency: our legal team asked whether logs from the canary pool will persist in the same retention tier as production. We need an assurance on 90-day retention and location in us-central.

Also — Marco and I would prefer two half-day training sessions for the integration team (one for platform/infra, one for product owners) rather than a single 45-minute session.

If you can respond to the three items above, we’ll confirm the 8/3 kickoff or propose alternatives.

Best,
Eleanor Briggs
Director, AI Platform
Labsuite.ai
eleanor.briggs@labsuite.ai

Subject: Re: Post-signature onramp: deployment commitment, canary gating, and training cadence

Eleanor — thanks, great questions. Answers below and small updates to the MAP: 

1) Capacity assumptions: we modeled the canary using a 900-token average sequence and 1.2s p95 latency baseline on the medium-density pool. That means the 5% cohort will need ~0.05 * your current QPS. We’ll include a small buffer in the MAP to avoid throttling.

2) Blackout windows: noted. We will not schedule any migrations or canary ramp activities between 2028-08-15 and 2028-08-18 and will avoid 2028-09-07.

3) Data residency & retention: logs from the canary pool will be stored in the us-central tenant with a 90-day retention by default. If you need longer, we can set up an archival export to a customer bucket.

Training cadence: we’ll split into two half-day sessions. Proposed slots attached in training-calendar.ics: Mon 8/7 (platform/infra), Tue 8/8 (product owners) — 1:00–4:00 PT each. Please confirm attendee lists and we’ll book the sessions.

I’ve attached an updated MAP that includes the capacity assumptions and the blackout window placemarkers. Next steps: once you confirm attendees and the kickoff, we’ll:

- Provision the canary pool (internal infra task, ETA 48 hours after kickoff).
- Share the rollback runbook and the test harness repo.
- Schedule the training sessions and deliver the training materials.

Thanks — I’ll plan to hold the 8/3 kickoff tentative and switch to 8/4 if you prefer.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Head of Customer Onboarding
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_Labsuite_v1.xlsx (v1.1 with capacity notes), training-calendar.ics
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 02 Aug 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-signature onramp: deployment commitment, canary gating, and training cadence

Eleanor / Monica — quick technical gating items from engineering: 

- Acceptance criteria for canary: <3% error rate on labeled calls, p95 latency within 1.5x baseline, and no KV-cache mismatch errors across consecutive requests.
- Rollback: automated traffic shift back to blue pool (30 min automated window) + manual human approval if any model state migration occurred.
- KMS note: Labsuite will need an HSM-backed key for production; canary will use a tenant key in KMS but not an HSM key. We can rehearse the HSM handover post-canary.

We’ll add these as gating rows in the MAP and include a short checklist for the runbook.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
